function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed for millennia.  The systematic scientific study of electricity began in the 16th‑17th centuries:

| Person | Contribution |
|--------|--------------|
| **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | Noted that rubbing amber produced static charge. |
| **William Gilbert** (1544–1603) | Published *De Magnete* (1600), distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coined the term “electricus.” |
| **Benjamin Franklin** (1706–1790) | Conducted kite experiments, proved that lightning is electrical, introduced the concept of positive/negative charges. |
| **Alessandro Volta** (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery) in 1800. |
| **Michael Faraday** (1791–1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction, laying the groundwork for electric generators and motors. |

So while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the modern understanding emerged through the cumulative work of many scientists over centuries.
